description.p: Dimmer lowers the brightness of individual monitors without changing the hardware backlight. A master control drives every configured screen, and each screen can also be adjusted or switched off on its own.

Optional screen identity numbers and boundaries make it easy to tell monitors apart. The tint colour is mixed into the dimming overlay for a warmer result, and the settings window can be excluded so it stays fully readable while everything behind it is dimmed.

The application also provides a top-bar indicator for opening and quitting, can start hidden, and supports autostart in native installations. On GNOME Wayland a small GNOME Shell extension renders the click-through overlay; the Rust application owns all settings and behaviour.
First Linux release: per-monitor dimming, master control, screen IDs, boundaries, tint, non-dimmable settings window, tray indicator, autostart and GNOME Shell integration.
